assertion: Enrollment in Texas public schools fell by more than 135,000 students this year, the largest single-year decline ever recorded in the state.
reason: Preliminary early-October 2026 TEA figure presented by Morath; the article itself calls it preliminary. Fox 4 and Community Impact report the same 135,000 and largest-ever. Estimate, matches agency figure.
warehouse_value: CCD through 2024-25 only; prior record in CCD series is 2020-21 at -122,592

assertion: Preliminary Texas Education Agency data shared Wednesday shows the state has lost nearly 212,000 students over the past two years.
reason: Estimate. TEA official 2024-25 5,544,255 minus about 5.33M is about 211-214k; 76,613 (TEA official) plus 135,000 is about 211,600.

assertion: Morath blamed low birthrates for much of the enrollment decline.
speaker: Mike Morath
reason: Morath said births are 'driving the train' (Fox 4, Community Impact), and Texas births did dip (364,360 in 2020-21 vs 378,664 in 2019). Caveat for framing: births recovered to 390,203 by 2025, so the dip alone is far too small for a 135,000 one-year loss; Morath also cited reduced migration and non-public options.
sql: SELECT "year", SUM(births) FROM census.pep_components_of_change WHERE state_fips='48' GROUP BY "year" ORDER BY "year"

Axios reports 70% were previously private or homeschooled.
